Full Advanced Tuning with REW

A complete DSP tune using REW measurements. It includes crossover setup, individual speaker EQ, level matching, time alignment and phase, and final EQ work.

Setting Ideal Crossovers

We measure each speaker’s natural roll-off to find crossover points that let it hand off smoothly to the next driver. We work around wide nulls and keep each speaker within its mechanical limits.

Single-Speaker EQ

We measure each speaker in isolation to see how cabin gain affects its response. We tame peaks and favor cuts over boosts to preserve headroom.

Level Matching

After individual speaker EQ, we measure each channel at the intended listening position and adjust its level so the speakers play in balance. Then we move on to timing and phase.

Time Alignment and Phase

We measure from the intended listening position to set precise delays for a tight center image and bass that sounds like it’s coming from up front. Tone sweeps show where speakers add together or cancel. We adjust delay or polarity as needed so the drivers hand off smoothly.

Final EQ Work

For the final EQ passes, we measure one full side at a time, then measure the full system together. We make all final adjustments on the system-wide EQ to preserve the phase and time alignment between speakers.

In-Person Tuning

Bring a drivable, insured vehicle with a fully installed and working sound system and DSP.

Remote Tuning
  • Sound system and DSP. Both should be fully installed and working. Having the gains set ahead of time is preferred. Our tuner can adjust them based on the measurements.
  • Measurement microphone. Use a proper measurement mic. Our budget pick is the miniDSP UMIK-1.
  • Audio source. Have a source that can play the test files we’ll send you.
  • Laptop and software. Set up a fresh user account on your laptop. Install RustDesk for remote desktop access, REW, and your DSP’s control software. Have a stable internet connection.
  • Quiet location and battery power. Use a reasonably quiet spot. We recommend tuning with the engine off, so have a battery charger available during or after the session.
  • Someone at the vehicle. Set the seat to your comfortable listening position. Move the mic around where your head would be for pink-noise EQ measurements, then place it at the center of that position for alignment and sweeps.
